Create an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican using html/3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- To look at the page yourself, serve it locally and screenshot it in headless Chrome (Chrome is
  installed, and a driver such as puppeteer-core or playwright can be npm-installed here). Save every
  screenshot you look at as a .jpg file, never .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a
  long session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

# Surfing Pelican

An animated, non-interactive 3D scene of a pelican surfing a curling ocean wave, built with HTML + Three.js.

## Files

- `index.html` — entry point, loads `main.js` as an ES module
- `main.js` — all scene code (pelican, surfboard, ocean, wave, foam, spray, clouds, camera)

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm run dev    # or: npx serve .  /  python3 -m http.server
```

Then open the printed local URL in a browser. There are no controls — the pelican carves, flaps, and the water moves on its own. Best viewed full-screen.

## Package check

```sh
npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null
```

The page needs no network requests and uses no storage (localStorage/cookies), so it runs offline in a sandboxed iframe.

## Run

`index.html` imports `three` by package name, so it must be bundled before it can run in a browser:

```sh
npm install
npx esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=bundle.js
```

Point any static server at a page that loads `bundle.js` as a module (or use your bundler), then open it in a browser. There are no controls — the pelican carves, flaps, and the water moves on its own. Best viewed full-screen.

Built an animated, non-interactive surfing pelican in HTML/Three.js.

**What it is:** A procedural 3D scene — a white pelican with a long orange beak, throat pouch, sunglasses, and webbed feet stands on a teal surfboard and rides a translucent curling wave. It carves back and forth along the wave face with lean, bob, wing-flap balancing, head sway, and pouch jiggle. Around it: animated ocean with sine swell, a foam lip on the crest, spray particles trailing the board, a wake, drifting clouds, a distant palm island, sun, and a slow drifting camera. No controls or pointer handlers — it plays on its own.

**Files:**
- [index.html](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-11-10-164616-surfing-pelican/muse-ember-1.0-mc-medium-20261110-164616/work/index.html) — entry point, inline styles, `<script type="module" src="main.js">`
- [main.js](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-11-10-164616-surfing-pelican/muse-ember-1.0-mc-medium-20261110-164616/work/main.js) — all scene code, `import * as THREE from "three"`, no CDN or import map, no storage APIs
- [README.md](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-11-10-164616-surfing-pelican/muse-ember-1.0-mc-medium-20261110-164616/work/README.md)

**Verified:** `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` succeeds; the bundled page was served locally and screenshotted in headless Chrome (as JPGs) across multiple frames, confirming the animation loop, wave, foam, and spray render without page errors.
